text:
Pittsburgh and San Jose arrive with the same 1-4-0 record over their last five, and both are looking for a way out. The Penguins lost 5-2 at Anaheim three days ago, where Cutter Gauthier scored three, and they're playing without Bryan Rust, with Tommy Novak now skating beside Crosby and Rakell. The Sharks snapped a five-game winless run with a shootout win over the Islanders on Monday, and they're without Igor Chernyshov, so Michael Misa has moved up beside Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith.

The chance numbers favor Pittsburgh. At five on five, the Penguins have taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side gets) in their games, and San Jose 45%. The Sharks also take 4.5 penalties a game, which keeps feeding power plays. In net, projected starters Arturs Silovs (PIT) and Yaroslav Askarov (SJS) tell different stories: Silovs is at -2.6 goals saved above expected this season, Askarov at +5.7, though Askarov was at -19.4 last year and Silovs at -12.8.

Crosby, who moved to sixth on the all-time scoring list this week, is at 36% to score and 66% for a point. Celebini is our best-looking Shark at 46% to score, one point from 200 for his career. Among our under-the-radar picks, Nick Robertson (PIT) has created 2.5 expected goals over his last 10 games from the third line, and Ben Kindel (PIT) sits at 50% for a point against a Sharks defense that allows the most chances.
